description: Review F3 + CF1 (consensus spec+testing). Store.safe_decode/2 with opts=[] decodes UNSAFE (atom-resurrecting) despite its name — rename or flip the default to fail closed, making unsafe opt-in at the two documented carve-out sites (read_v2 envelope, load_tracer_edges manifest readers). CF1: those non-safe carve-outs have no positive regression-guard test — add tests pinning that a fresh-BEAM decode of a foreign-module artifact still succeeds there (the justification for keeping them unsafe), so a future blanket-[:safe] sweep fails loudly.

comments.text:
ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: small
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
Both halves remain. Full mandate:

1. Fail-closed default (lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex):
   - Line 358: change `defp safe_decode(bin, opts \\ []) do` to `defp safe_decode(bin, opts \\ [:safe]) do` (or rename the pair to `decode/2` + an explicit `decode_unsafe/1`; flipping the default is the smaller edit).
   - Line 238 (inside `read_v2/1`): change `{:ok, term} <- safe_decode(bin) do` to an EXPLICIT unsafe opt-in, e.g. `{:ok, term} <- safe_decode(bin, []) do`, keeping the existing justification comment at store.ex:231-237 immediately above it.
   - Line 295 (inside `read_status/1`): may stay `safe_decode(bin, [:safe])` or drop to `safe_decode(bin)`; keep the `[:safe]` justification comment at store.ex:290-294 intact either way. End state: no call site gets atom-resurrecting behavior implicitly.

2. Positive regression guards (CF1) — a foreign/never-interned atom must still DECODE SUCCESSFULLY at each documented unsafe carve-out, so a future blanket `[:safe]` sweep fails loudly:
   a. test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs, inside `describe "v2 envelope round trip"` (line 150): add a test that builds v2-envelope ETF bytes whose `:files` entry carries a `:module` atom that was never interned in this VM — reuse the existing private helper `hostile_atom_binary/1` (store_test.exs:479-484), which plants the name by byte-patching a same-length placeholder so `String.to_atom/1` is never called on it — write those bytes to the artifact path, then assert `{:ok, envelope} = Store.read_v2(path)` AND that the resurrected atom is now reachable via `String.to_existing_atom(name)`. Tag it with the existing `@describetag spec: ["specled.coverage_capture.store_v2_envelope", "specled.coverage_capture.store_v2_legacy_rejection"]` or an explicit `@tag spec:` (see item 3).
   b. Tracer-manifest carve-out: add the mirror guard for the raw readers. Cheapest single site is `SpecLedEx.Realization.Implementation`'s `read_tracer_etf/1` (lib/specled_ex/realization/implementation.ex:519-529), reachable from tests via `load_tracer_edges/2`'s `opts[:tracer_manifest]` override (implementation.ex:495-497, 513-516) — write a manifest file whose caller/callee MFA key names a never-interned module atom (same byte-patch technique; do NOT use `Module.concat`, which interns) and assert the edge map comes back non-empty with that key present. Anchor tag: `specled.compiler_tracer.etf_read_direct` (.spec/specs/compiler_tracer.spec.md:160-165) or `specled.implementation_tier.ghost_edges_filtered`. If the reviewer wants all three raw readers pinned, the same fixture can be driven through `Mix.Tasks.Spec.Triangle` (lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex:112-130) and `SpecLedEx.Review.CoverageClosure` (lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:38-55), but both are `defp` with no injection seam — the Implementation site is the one with a test hook.

3. Spec ownership: no requirement in .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md states any decode-atom policy (`grep -rn "binary_to_term\|:safe\]" .spec/` hits only compiler_tracer.spec.md:163 and two ADRs). The new tests need an owning clause or they repeat the specled_-npo "test ahead of the requirement" class. Add one additive requirement to the `spec-requirements` block of .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md (e.g. `specled.coverage_capture.decode_atom_policy`, priority: must, stability: evolving) stating: v1 `read/1` and the `last_run.status` sidecar decode with `[:safe]` and shall reject never-interned atoms; `read_v2/1` decodes without `[:safe]` because an ingested/merged aggregate envelope may legitimately name a module absent from this BEAM, and shall return `{:ok, envelope}` in that case. Append after the existing `specled.coverage_capture.store_v2_legacy_rejection` requirement (.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:419-427). Purely additive → append-only safe.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex, test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs, .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md, test/specled_ex/realization/implementation_test.exs

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION HASHES — low risk, do not skip the reasoning: `.spec/realization_hashes.json` has a single tier key, `api_boundary`, and it DOES contain `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Store.read_v2/1`, `.read_status/1`, `.read/1`, `.load/1`. But the api_boundary hasher hashes the resolved function HEAD only — lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex:5-13 documents it as "stable under formatting changes, variable renames, and line-number shifts ... but changing under arity, arg pattern shape, or literal default argument changes". All the edits above are BODY edits to `read_v2/1` plus a change to the private, unbound `safe_decode/2`. `safe_decode/2` has no realization binding (it is `defp`, absent from realization_hashes.json and from .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md's realized_by lists at :131-148). => no drift expected. If you instead RENAME/re-signature any public Store function, that WILL trip the drift gate and needs a `.spec/realization_hashes.json` baseline update — prefer the flip-the-default option to avoid it.

SPEC-FILE CONTENTION — .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md is edited by at least three tickets in this set: specled_-npo (rewrites the `specled.coverage_capture.envelope_meta` statement at :551-565), specled_-xkn.2 (coverage-provenance documentation, same subject), and this ticket (appends a new requirement near :419-427). All three edit the same `spec-requirements` YAML block. Land them in one pass or expect textual conflicts; ordering does not matter semantically since all three are additive/statement-local.

TEST-FILE CONTENTION — test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs: specled_-26g's mandate (unique-dir the read_status + load sidecar tests) already appears SATISFIED in this tree (setup blocks at store_test.exs:156-168 and :330-344 both build `Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "store_v2_#{unique_integer}")` / `"store_status_#{unique_integer}"` with `on_exit(&File.rm_rf!/1)`), but if 26g is re-opened it edits the same describe-block setups my new test sits inside. test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs is specled_-asb's file (merge_edges property at :241-293) — my tracer guard is a separate test, but same file. test/mix/tasks/spec_triangle_test.exs is specled_-b23's file if you choose to pin the spec.triangle reader too; prefer the Implementation seam to avoid that collision entirely.

NO BLOCKING DEPENDENCY — this ticket does not need any other ticket to land first.

GATE — the new tests must carry `@tag spec:`/`@describetag spec:` or the tagged_tests-consistency leg of `mix spec.check` will flag them; that leg is known-flaky under load (per project memory), so re-run before concluding failure. Adding a requirement without at least one `covers:`/tagged test will fire the coverage/verification legs, so land requirement + tests together in the same commit.

CAUTION FOR THE IMPLEMENTER — do not build the never-interned atom with `String.to_atom/1` or `Module.concat/1`; both intern it and silently void the guard. Use the existing byte-patch helper `hostile_atom_binary/1` (test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs:479-484) or copy its technique; if you promote it for reuse across store_test.exs and the tracer/implementation test, put it in test/support rather than duplicating.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate (items 1-3), which is what you implement.

## STALE CONTENTION NOTES — the admission predates four merges
Since that admission was written, specled_-26g, specled_-npo, specled_-asb and
specled_-chb have all LANDED on the epic branch. Consequences for you:
- `test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs`: 26g rewrote the `describe "load/1"` setup and
  it now uses `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0`, NOT `System.unique_integer`. The
  admission describes the pre-26g shape. Re-read the file.
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md`: npo appended a `read_v2/1` clause to
  `specled.coverage_capture.envelope_meta` and extended its scenario. Line numbers moved.
- Every line number the admission cites has shifted. Anchor on CONTENT, not line numbers.
- If YOU allocate any new tmp root, use `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` — that is
  now the ADR-stated rule for new allocations (specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach,
  amended by specled_-ehv).

## Allowed touches
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex`
- `test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md` — item 3's ONE additive requirement, appended
  after `specled.coverage_capture.store_v2_legacy_rejection`. Purely additive is
  append-only safe.
- `test/specled_ex/realization/implementation_test.exs` — item 2b's mirror guard.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `lib/specled_ex/realization/implementation.ex` — you consume `load_tracer_edges/2`'s
  `opts[:tracer_manifest]` test hook; do not change the production reader.
- `test/mix/tasks/spec_triangle_test.exs` — specled_-b23's file. The admission offers
  pinning the spec.triangle and CoverageClosure readers too; DO NOT. Both are `defp` with
  no injection seam, and the Implementation site is the one with a test hook. Use it and
  avoid the collision entirely.
- `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs` — specled_-asb and specled_-ehv both landed
  there; your tracer guard belongs in implementation_test.exs per item 2b.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (orchestrator consolidates once at the end), `VERSION`,
  `.spec/realization_hashes.json`, `.spec/state.json`.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent) — the api_boundary constraint is the one to respect
- PREFER FLIPPING THE DEFAULT (`safe_decode(bin, opts \\ [:safe])`) over renaming the
  pair. `.spec/realization_hashes.json` DOES carry `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Store.read_v2/1`,
  `.read_status/1`, `.read/1` and `.load/1`, but api_boundary hashes the resolved function
  HEAD only — stable under body edits, UNSTABLE under arity, arg-pattern or literal-default
  changes to a PUBLIC function. `safe_decode/2` is private and unbound, so changing its
  default is safe. Renaming or re-signaturing any public `Store` function WILL trip the
  drift gate. `git diff --stat -- .spec/realization_hashes.json` must be EMPTY.
- End state for item 1: NO call site gets atom-resurrecting behaviour implicitly. The
  `read_v2/1` site must opt IN explicitly, with the existing justification comment kept
  immediately above it.
- Item 3 is not optional. Without an owning requirement the new tests repeat the
  "test ahead of the requirement" class this epic already hit on specled_-npo.
- No new dependencies.

## FALSIFIABILITY BAR
The CF1 guards exist so that a future blanket `[:safe]` sweep FAILS LOUDLY. Prove they do:
1. After adding each guard, temporarily add `[:safe]` to the carve-out call site it
   protects (the `read_v2/1` decode, and the tracer-manifest raw read).
2. Confirm the corresponding guard goes RED. Paste the failure.
3. Revert. Confirm green.
Do this for BOTH guards (item 2a and item 2b). A guard that stays green under a blanket
`[:safe]` sweep is worthless — that sweep is the exact future event it is built to catch.
Record both mutations and reverts in the COMMIT MESSAGE.

Use the existing `hostile_atom_binary/1` helper for the never-interned atom. Do NOT use
`Module.concat` or `String.to_atom` to construct the test atom — both intern it, which
destroys the test.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs test/specled_ex/realization/implementation_test.exs`
3. `mix format --check-formatted`
4. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`
5. `git diff --stat -- .spec/realization_hashes.json` must be EMPTY.

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. The orchestrator owns
whole-system proof at the merge gate and PR CI.

Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/specled_ex/specled_-xkn.1/grok-k6s-xkn.1-impl-1/log

Files touched: lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex, test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs, test/specled_ex/realization/implementation_test.exs, .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md
Tests added: SpecLedEx.Coverage.StoreTest "read_v2 succeeds on an envelope whose :files name a never-interned module atom"; SpecLedEx.Realization.ImplementationTest "hashes_for_seeding loads a tracer_manifest whose keys name a never-interned module". Also retagged existing v1-read and read_status hostile tests under decode_atom_policy.
Verification stubs flipped: none (existing tagged_tests block for store_v2_* extended to cover new requirement specled.coverage_capture.decode_atom_policy; execute already true)
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs test/specled_ex/realization/implementation_test.exs; mix format --check-formatted; mix spec.check --no-run-commands; git diff --stat -- .spec/realization_hashes.json EMPTY; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1
Falsifiability: (1) read_v2 temporarily safe_decode(bin, [:safe]) → store guard RED with {:error, :invalid_artifact}; reverted green. (2) read_tracer_etf temporarily binary_to_term(binary, [:safe]) → tracer guard RED with ArgumentError on String.to_existing_atom; reverted green. Both recorded in commit message.
Epic lessons checked: [stale-spec] decode_atom_policy describes the shipped default+explicit-opt-in (not a rename); [stale-spec] rule is satisfiable by production paths; [untested-clause] CF1 inputs use never-interned atoms where safe vs unsafe DISAGREE; [other] mix format --check-formatted green; [other] completion posted to specled_-xkn.1.

Summary: Flipped private safe_decode/2 default to [:safe] (fail-closed). read_v2/1 now opts in explicitly with []; read_status uses the default. Added additive requirement decode_atom_policy plus positive CF1 guards for the two documented unsafe carve-outs (v2 envelope foreign module; tracer-manifest foreign module via Implementation's tracer_manifest test hook) so a future blanket [:safe] sweep fails loudly.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS

Session: b19669f0-1a1a-42a6-b6f8-39da90177a9c
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/b19669f0-1a1a-42a6-b6f8-39da90177a9c.jsonl

Findings:

- (a) Never-interned property HOLDS for both guards. Both use the byte-patch
  helper: store_test.exs:520 (pre-existing) and implementation_test.exs:628 (new,
  verbatim copy). The name is built as a STRING "hostile_never_interned_<N>" with
  N = System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]); only the same-length
  placeholder "xxx..." is ever passed to String.to_atom/1, and the real name is
  planted with :binary.replace/3 into the encoded ETF. No Module.concat, no
  String.to_atom on the hostile name, no atom literal in the source. The name is
  lowercase and un-prefixed, so it cannot collide with any Elixir module atom
  (those are "Elixir."-prefixed); grep over lib/ test/ .spec/ shows the string
  exists nowhere except these two helpers. N is VM-globally unique, so the two
  files cannot collide with each other even in the same VM.

- (b) Both guards go RED under the sweep they exist to catch (verified, then
  reverted; git status clean):
  * store.ex:239 safe_decode(bin, []) -> safe_decode(bin, [:safe]) =>
    exactly 1 failure, store_test.exs:355 "assert {:ok, envelope} = Store.read_v2(path)"
    got {:error, :invalid_artifact}.
  * implementation.ex:522 :erlang.binary_to_term(binary) -> ..., [:safe]) =>
    exactly 1 failure, implementation_test.exs:670 ArgumentError "not an already
    existing atom" from String.to_existing_atom/1 (the rescue-to-%{} fallback in
    read_tracer_etf/1 is silent, so this line is the only detector).
  Both files green as committed (seeds 355568, 347937, 670205, 1).

- (c) Store guard assertion is STRONG: store_test.exs:356-358 asserts
  {:ok, envelope}, matches out envelope.files' :module, and pins
  String.to_existing_atom(hostile_name) == mod, i.e. "decoded AND the atom now
  exists AND it is the one in the envelope".

- (c) RECOMMENDATION (not blocking) — tracer guard is weaker than it reads.
  implementation_test.exs:667 `assert Map.has_key?(hashes, "A")` is NOT
  load-bearing: under the [:safe] mutation the test sailed past it with an empty
  edge map and only died at line 670. The test never confirms the decoded edge
  map is non-empty or keyed by the foreign atom — it only proves the decode
  interned the atom, not that the manifest reached world.tracer_edges. I probed a
  cheap strengthening and it works: with
    clean = Implementation.hashes_for_seeding(subjects, nil, tracer_manifest: write_fixture_etf!(root))
    empty = Implementation.hashes_for_seeding(subjects, nil, tracer_manifest: Path.join(root, "nope.etf"))
  the observed result is {hashes == clean, hashes == empty} = {true, false}.
  So `assert hashes == clean` + `refute hashes == empty` would prove the foreign
  manifest was actually consumed, not merely decoded. write_fixture_etf!/1 already
  exists at implementation_test.exs:606.

- (c) NIT: the store v2 guard has no pre-condition proof that the atom is absent
  before the read. implementation_test.exs:661 does exactly that
  (assert_raise ArgumentError, fn -> String.to_existing_atom(hostile_name) end).
  Adding the same line before Store.read_v2/1 makes the store guard
  self-evidencing rather than relying on the helper's docstring.

- (d) No isolation hazard. The v2 guard is the only test that interns a hostile
  atom; the two negative guards (store_test.exs:96, :429) assert absence of THEIR
  OWN unique name, and monotonic unique_integer makes name reuse impossible. No
  test anywhere asserts a fixed atom name is absent. Ordering-independent:
  confirmed green across 4 seeds.

- (e) Temp isolation OK. The tracer guard writes xref_hostile.etf into the
  per-test `root` from the pre-existing setup at implementation_test.exs:73-80;
  it allocates NO new root, so TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 is not owed here. Note
  (pre-existing, not this ticket): that root uses :erlang.unique_integer, which is
  VM-local, not cross-VM. Same for the v2 describe's store_v2_ tmp dir
  (store_test.exs:163). Neither was introduced or worsened here.

- (f) Confirmed retag-only. The v1-read hostile test (store_test.exs:83) and the
  read_status hostile test (store_test.exs:419) gained exactly one `+ @tag spec:`
  line each in the diff; zero assertion lines changed, nothing weakened.

- (g) No Process.sleep, no spawned/unmanaged processes, no shared-tmp writes in
  either new test.

- WARNING — over-tagging widens the requirement's attestation set beyond the
  guard. store_test.exs:151-155 adds decode_atom_policy to the v2
  @describetag, and TagScanner expands @describetag spec: lists to every test in
  the block. That makes ~10 unrelated v2 tests (garbage bytes, non-map :meta,
  legacy artifact, ...) attest specled.coverage_capture.decode_atom_policy. The
  addition is also redundant: the new test carries its own @tag spec: at
  store_test.exs:332, which overrides the describetag at runtime. Net effect —
  delete the CF1 guard and the requirement still reads as attested by 10 tests
  that never exercise atom decode policy. Recommend dropping decode_atom_policy
  from the @describetag and leaving it on the three per-test @tag lines only
  (:82, :332, :418), which is exactly the set `--only spec:...decode_atom_policy`
  selects today.

- mix spec.check --no-run-commands: pass (validate errors=0 warnings=0,
  branch findings 13 info / 0 error / 0 warning). etf_read_direct exists at
  compiler_tracer.spec.md:160 and is on an execute:true tagged_tests leg
  (:264); the requirement's own wording ("via :erlang.binary_to_term/1") makes
  the new guard a direct falsifier for the arity-1 clause.

- Working tree left clean (only pre-existing untracked .grok/sandbox.toml).
